SI-4_title.answer: Developmental trajectories of neuroanatomical alterations associated with the 16p11.2 Copy Number Variations

DC-1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: NIHPD (NIH MRI Study of Normal Brain Development) used as normative reference data for brain growth. EU (European 16p11.2 consortium) and SVIP (Simons Variation in Individuals Project) datasets used for 16p11.2 CNV carriers and controls for case-control analysis.
DC-1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "As normative reference data for brain growth, we used the multi-site longitudinal data from Objective 1 ... of the publicly available NIHPD project" ... "Cross-sectional data was acquired in 2 different cohorts (the European -EU 16p11.2 consortium and the Simons VIP -SVIP study in North America)"

DC-2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: NIHPD was used to build the normative developmental model for Z-scoring. The normative model built on NIHPD was then applied to calculate Z-scores for the 16p11.2 CNV carriers and controls from EU and SVIP cohorts for case-control analysis.
DC-2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "As normative reference data for brain growth, we used the multi-site longitudinal data from Objective 1 ... of the publicly available NIHPD project" ... "To compute Z-scores that normalize for the effect of growth and sex in a pediatric population, we modeled the effect of those 2 variables in the NIHPD normative dataset." ... "Using the mean and the estimated standard deviation of the model we were able to compute Z-scores ... for the 16p11.2 and control participants"

model-1.model-name: Mixed-effects normative model for brain growth

DC-3_hc_n_of_each_normative_model.detail: The normative model was built using all 339 children from NIHPD cohort. The paper does not describe a separate train/validation/test split for the normative model; all NIHPD subjects were used to fit the mixed-effects model. Total of 874 scans from longitudinal acquisitions (2 or 3 time points per subject).
DC-3_hc_n_of_each_normative_model.supporting_text: "The normative model (Aubert-Broche et al., 2011) used data from 339 children (179 females and 160 males), scanned longitudinally at 2 or 3 time points, with approximately 24 months between scans and mean age at first scan of 11.0 years, for a total of 874 scans."

DC-4_age_info_of_each_normative_model.detail: Mean age at first scan was 11.0 years. Age range for enrolment was 4.5 to 18.5 years. SD, median, and IQR were not reported. The age model was centered at 13 years (mean age of NIHPD cohort according to the model description).
DC-4_age_info_of_each_normative_model.supporting_text: "The normative model (Aubert-Broche et al., 2011) used data from 339 children (179 females and 160 males), scanned longitudinally at 2 or 3 time points, with approximately 24 months between scans and mean age at first scan of 11.0 years" ... "Objective 1 (i.e. initial time-point for enrolment from 4.5 to 18.5 years)" ... "Age was not divided into bins, but was considered as a continuous variable and was centered at 13 years - the mean age of NIHPD cohort."

DC-5_sex_info_of_each_normative_model.detail: All 339 NIHPD subjects were used for the normative model. 179 females (52.8%) and 160 males (47.2%).
DC-5_sex_info_of_each_normative_model.supporting_text: "The normative model (Aubert-Broche et al., 2011) used data from 339 children (179 females and 160 males), scanned longitudinally at 2 or 3 time points"
